behavior.laps.note:
InputError: detect_laps(method='auto') counts laps around a loop, but this environment has no loop: its track graph has no cycle, or its area has no hole to run around.
Why: on a track, a tree maze or in an open arena the animal can always come back the way it went, so no lap goes round a loop and the laps found would have direction 'unknown'.
Fix: for back-and-forth runs on a linear track or arm, use detect_trials(env, times, positions, regions=[start, end]); to segment round trips against a template, pass method='reference' with reference_lap=, which reports each round trip's direction along the track as 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

position: ValueError: Position series 'SpatialSeries' has 3 columns and declares unit 'centimeters; centimeters/second', which is not one length or pixel unit.
Why: a column may hold speed or another non-spatial value; using every column would bin it as a spatial axis of a 3-D environment.
Fix: pass columns= with the spatial columns, e.g. columns=[0, 1] for x and y, or columns=[0, 1, 2] if all are spatial. The series describes its data as: 'Video frames taken at 30fps - row1:xpos row2:ypos row3:velocity'.

All 57 units are silent from 6273.7 s to 7172.8 s (899 s) while position is tracked. If the electrophysiology was not recording then, pass spike_window=(start, stop) so that time is excluded from occupancy.
322424/322424 spike_times (100%) across all neurons fell outside the position time window [2322.5, 11691.4]; spike_times.min()=2.32251e+06 spike_times.max()=1.16914e+07. The spike times span 9.36884e+06 and reach 1.16914e+07, about 1000 times the 9368.85 s of times: if spike_times are in milliseconds, divide them by 1000. Check that spike_times and times share units (both seconds). Dropped spikes do not contribute. Set warn_on_drop=False to suppress this warning.

bin_size=2.5 is at least the per-axis data extent [1.137, 1.035] in every dimension.
Why: this produces very few bins, and it is often a units mistake: positions in m but bin_size meant in cm, for example.
Fix: check that bin_size and positions use the same units, then use a bin_size well below the data extent, such as bin_size=0.02

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, min_speed=4.0, epochs), so occupancy is zero in every bin. Fix: pass max_gap=None to disable gap gating; check that min_speed=4.0 is in the positions' length units per second; check that epochs overlap `times` (same clock, seconds).

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, min_speed=4.0, epochs), so the rate map is empty. Fix: pass max_gap=None to disable gap gating; check that min_speed=4.0 is in the positions' length units per second; check that epochs overlap `times` (same clock, seconds).

Creating large grid with shape (47, 43, 94) (189,974 bins). Estimated memory usage: 258.0 MB.
Why: allocating this grid may consume substantial memory.
Fix: increase bin_size; this grid has 189,974 bins. For example, use bin_size=2.0 in the same units as positions, and check that positions has shape (n_samples, n_dims)

ValueError: Environment.occupancy got positions with shape (80087, 3), but this environment's bins are 2-D, so positions needs shape (n_positions, 2).
Why: each row is one position, with one column per coordinate of env.bin_centers.
Fix: pass an array of shape (n_positions, 2), one row per position

InputError: Invalid times/positions passed to compute_spatial_rates():
- Got positions with shape (80087, 3), but this environment's bins are 2-D, so positions needs shape (n_positions, 2).
Why: each interval [times[k], times[k+1]) is weighted by its duration, so mis-shaped, unsorted or repeated timestamps give wrong numbers.
Fix: pass times as a sorted 1-D array of numeric timestamps in seconds, without repeats, with one numeric positions row per timestamp.
